name: psf/requests v2.32.3 retrieval suite
notes: Natural-language questions with hand-checked line ranges at the pinned commit. 'author' records who wrote each query: queries written by someone who had just read the function list leak symbol knowledge, so results should also be reported per author. Queries with author 'claude-heldout' were written after the BM25 change was decided and were not used to make it; they share the author bias of the first 31 (same writer, who has read the code). Queries with author 'stackoverflow' are real question titles, copied verbatim from the top-voted python-requests questions on Stack Overflow (id = question id). They were picked in vote order by a fixed rule (keep a question only if one place in the requests source implements what it asks about; skip install/environment errors, comparisons with other libraries and repeated topics; stop at 15), set before any retrieval run on them. Ground truth was chosen by Claude, who has read the code. 'docs_answers' (Stack Overflow queries only) lists user-docs sections that directly answer the question as asked; they count for the separate answered@k metric, not for code recall. Sections were chosen by heading from the docs table of contents, after the retrieval results for these queries had already been seen, so they may carry some bias. The two error-message questions (no connection adapters, max retries exceeded) have no docs section that explains them and get none. Queries with author 'stackoverflow-2' are a second, untouched set for the fusion test in eval/fusion_replication_preregistration.md. Same source and rule, continuing in vote order from rank 25 (the rank after the last of the first 15) in a list fetched on 2026-11-15 and saved as eval/sources/so_python_requests_by_votes_2026-11-15.json; so_vote_rank is the 0-based position in that list. Ranks 25-840 were examined and 40 kept. 'Topic already covered' was applied mechanically: a question is skipped if the function implementing it is already the ground truth of an earlier kept Stack Overflow question. Ground truth and docs_answers for these 40 were written before any retrieval run on them; 28 have a docs answer. Queries with authors 'stackoverflow-3' and 'github-issues' are the two untouched sets for the routing test in eval/routing_preregistration.md, split by the production router (HybridCodeRetriever.compute_dynamic_alpha): every 'stackoverflow-3' title is a plain question and every 'github-issues' title is an identifier question. 'stackoverflow-3': same Stack Overflow list and rule, continuing from rank 841 (pages 11-15 were appended to the saved list for this); ranks 841-1352 were examined and 40 kept. 'github-issues': issue titles, verbatim, from psf/requests issues sorted by comments, saved as eval/sources/psf_requests_issues_by_comments_2026-11-15.json; issue_comment_rank is the 0-based position in that list and id is gh_<issue number>. Ranks 0-408 were examined and 30 kept. The repeat rule applies within each set only. Ground truth and docs_answers for all 70 were written before any retrieval run on them; 33 of the 40 plain and 16 of the 30 identifier questions have a docs answer. Queries with authors 'stackoverflow-4' and 'github-history' are the two untouched sets for the scope_gate test in eval/scope_gate_preregistration.md. 'stackoverflow-4': same Stack Overflow list and rule, continuing from rank 1353 (pages 16-25 were appended to the saved list); ranks 1353-2395 were examined and 60 kept, plain and identifier questions alike; ground truth is source code. 'github-history': issue titles from the saved psf/requests list that report behaviour changed between versions or name a test, kept only if HISTORY.md at v2.32.3 has an entry describing the change (ground truth = that bullet's lines) or the test exists (ground truth = that test function). For these, docs_answers holds the implementing code where one function implements it, so answered@k also counts finding the code. All 1,000 listed issues were examined and 23 qualified (21 changelog entries, 2 tests). Labels for all 83 were written before any retrieval run on them.
